has_dead_or_redundant_code.instructions: Does this PHP file contain dead code, unused functions, unreachable branches, commented-out logic blocks, debug output calls (var_dump, print_r, error_log), or variables that are assigned but never read?

criteria.true: All functions are called from somewhere meaningful, no debug output, no commented-out implementation blocks, no unreachable code after returns
criteria.false: Contains one or more: unused function definitions, commented-out logic, var_dump/print_r calls, variables that are set but never used, unreachable branches

violates_single_responsibility.instructions: Does this PHP file handle more than one distinct responsibility? A single responsibility violation occurs when the same file performs two or more of: database queries, session/auth enforcement, email sending, HTML rendering, business logic calculation, file upload handling, API calls to external services.

criteria.true: File has exactly one clear responsibility — either it is a controller, a pure view template, a data access layer, a service function library, or a security utility
criteria.false: File mixes two or more of: SQL queries + HTML output, auth checks + data mutation + email dispatch, presentation + business rules

lacks_php_type_safety.instructions: Does this PHP file use PHP 8.x strict type declarations? Look for: missing parameter types on functions that accept strings/ints/arrays, missing return types, loose equality comparisons (== vs ===), absent null handling (?string, mixed), and missing strict_types declaration.

criteria.true: Functions declare typed parameters and return types, strict_types=1 is present or types are consistently applied, null coalescing and strict equality are used
criteria.false: Functions lack typed parameters/returns, loose comparisons (== instead of ===) are common, no strict_types declaration, or untyped variables are mixed with business logic

primary_refactor_action.instructions: Based on the code's overall structure and the issues above, what is the single most impactful refactoring action needed? Choose 'none' if the file is reasonably clean for a PHP 8.2 project.

criteria.none: File is reasonably clean with clear structure, no significant tech debt, and well-scoped responsibilities
criteria.split_monolith: File is very large (typically >30KB) and handles multiple unrelated concerns that should be decomposed into separate modules or layers
criteria.extract_services: File contains reusable business logic functions that are mixed with controller or presentation code and should be moved to a dedicated service layer
criteria.extract_view_template: File mixes PHP controller logic (DB queries, auth, session) directly with HTML output and needs a clean controller/view separation
criteria.simplify_logic: File contains deeply nested conditionals, excessively long functions (>50 lines), or complex branching that could be simplified with guard clauses and named helpers
criteria.remove_dead_code: File has demonstrably unused functions, commented-out code blocks, debug output calls, or dead variable assignments that should be deleted
criteria.add_type_declarations: File lacks PHP 8.2 typed parameters and return types but is otherwise structurally clean and only needs type safety improvements

spaghetti_severity.instructions: How urgently does this PHP file need refactoring due to technical debt, complexity, or structural problems?
criteria: Production-clean: single clear responsibility, well-typed, no dead code, easy to read and maintain
Minor polish needed: mostly clean but has a few inconsistencies, loose types, or small dead code sections
Noticeable tech debt: multiple responsibilities mixed, missing types, some dead code, but still functional
High maintenance risk: large monolith or tightly coupled code causing clear structural problems
Critical spaghetti: god object or deeply tangled code requiring immediate decomposition to remain maintainable
